opener_episode.title: The Dark Side of the Nightclub Business | Money, Power & Secrets
opener_episode.why: Most recent episode, and its 'money, power and secrets of a cash-rich luxury business' frame is the closest bridge to Avery's world (celebrity and high-net-worth buyers, outlandish requests). Stronger alternative hook if the pitch leads with a shared guest: Cox previously ran 'The REAL Story Behind War Dogs | David Packouz' (date unverified), and Packouz has also been Avery's guest on ArtLife.

angles.headline: How the art world gets conned: fakes, forgeries and fake buyers, from a dealer who sells blue-chip work
angles.pitch: Avery has sold blue-chip art online since 2015 at eight-figure-a-year scale and can explain from the legit side how buyers spot (or miss) fraud and why art attracts con men.
angles.builds_on: Show's core con-man / fraud theme; an earlier Cox episode on a most-wanted counterfeiter (Apple episode id 1000745642645, date unverified)

angles.headline: Michael Cohen's prison badge as an NFT: crime memorabilia meets the NFT boom
angles.pitch: Avery was behind ArtGrails, which sold Michael Cohen's prison badge as an NFT (covered by Vanity Fair, 2021), a natural story for an audience that loves white-collar-crime characters.
angles.builds_on: White-collar / federal-prison storylines that run through the show (Cox's own fraud history; Whitey Bulger FBI episode, Sep 29 2026)

angles.headline: From War Dogs to the art world: the David Packouz connection
angles.pitch: Cox has interviewed David Packouz, and Avery has hosted him on ArtLife; Avery can talk about the hustlers, collectors and characters that a high-end art business attracts.
angles.builds_on: Cox's 'The REAL Story Behind War Dogs | David Packouz' episode; Sep 30 2026 nightclub-money episode

booking.route: Guest email and Google Form posted by the show (surfaced via a search snippet of the YouTube channel's community tab; not seen on an official website).
booking.source: https://invidious.cleberg.net/channel/UC3_qYh4foNgVXI7NzcuxlCA/community (mirror of the Matthew Cox YouTube community tab, channel UC3_qYh4foNgVXI7NzcuxlCA)

format: Long-form, video-first interview show (YouTube channel plus audio on Apple/Spotify), produced by Rhapsody Voices per Apple listing; near-daily episodes, 1,000+ total. Guests are mostly ex-criminals, cops, agents and journalists telling crime stories. Recording location/in-person vs remote unverified (Cox is Tampa-area based per prior research). Rephonic estimate ~21K-85K listens per episode.
red_flags: Guest profile is overwhelmingly criminals/law enforcement; Avery is a legit dealer, so the pitch must be framed around fraud, con men and crime-adjacent stories (ArtGrails/Cohen badge, Packouz), not a business story. Booking email was found only via a search snippet of a YouTube community post, not on an official site; confirm before use. The guest form was posted for specific topical calls (e.g., Diddy raid, Boeing whistleblower) and may be outdated.
notes: Episode dates come from search summaries of podcast directories (Sept 25-30, 2026); per-episode URLs weren't returned, so the show URL is used. The Packouz episode was confirmed by a search summary but its date and URL are unverified. Known feeder to This Past Weekend w/ Theo Von (per master list). Cox also appears in the 2026 TV series 'Inside the Mind of a Con Artist' (S1E1), which features an art forger (Shaun Greenhalgh) in another episode; this may help the art-fraud angle.
